sentences.zh: 元稹元稹，字微之，河南人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen, style name Weizhi, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, whose courtesy name was Weizhi, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 後魏昭成皇帝，稹十代祖也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng of Later Wei was Zhen's tenth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng of the Northern Wei was his tenth-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書、昌平公巖，六代祖也。

translations.literal: Yan, Minister of War and Duke of Changping, was his sixth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor was Yan, who had served as Minister of War and been enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖延景，岐州參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yanjing was a staff officer in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yanjing had held the post of military aide in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖悱，南頓丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was magistrate of Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fei had served as magistrate of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 父寬，比部郎中、舒王府長史，以稹貴，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was a director in the Ministry of Justice and senior administrator of the Prince of Shu's household; because of Zhen's eminence, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan had been a director in the Ministry of Justice and senior administrator of the Prince of Shu's household; when Zhen rose to prominence, Kuan was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稹八歲喪父。

translations.literal: Zhen lost his father at the age of eight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was only eight when his father died.

sentences.zh: 其母鄭夫人，賢明婦人也；

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Zheng, was a wise and worthy woman;
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zheng, was a woman of wisdom and virtue;

sentences.zh: 家貧，為稹自授書，教之書學。

translations.literal: The family was poor; she personally taught Zhen the classics and instructed him in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Though the household was poor, she taught him the classics herself and trained him in letters.

sentences.zh: 稹九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine Zhen could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of nine he could already compose prose.

sentences.zh: 十五兩經擢第。

translations.literal: At fifteen he passed the examinations in both Classics.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the civil service examinations in both of the Confucian Classics.

sentences.zh: 二十四調判入第四等，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At twenty-four his provincial assessment placed him in the fourth grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he qualified at the fourth grade in the provincial assessment and was made a proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 二十八應制舉才識兼茂、明於體用科，登第者十八人，稹為第一，元和元年四月也。

translations.literal: At twenty-eight he entered the special examination for men of outstanding talent and practical understanding; of the eighteen who passed, Zhen ranked first, in the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-eight he sat for the special "Outstanding Talent and Practical Understanding" examination; eighteen candidates passed, and Zhen took first place—in April of the first year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 制下，除右拾遺。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, he was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment edict followed, and he was named Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 稹性鋒銳，見事風生。

translations.literal: Zhen's nature was sharp; he seized on affairs as swiftly as wind arises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was quick and incisive by nature, grasping affairs the moment they arose.

sentences.zh: 既居諫垣，不欲碌碌自滯，事無不言，即日上疏論諫職。

translations.literal: Once he held a remonstrance post, he did not wish to linger in mediocrity; nothing passed without his speaking out, and that very day he submitted a memorial on the duties of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed in the remonstrance bureau, he refused to settle into routine obscurity; he spoke up on every matter and that very day submitted a memorial on the proper conduct of remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 又以前時王叔文、王伾以猥褻待詔，蒙幸太子，永貞之際，大撓朝政。

translations.literal: He also noted that earlier Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi, though base men awaiting summons at court, had won the crown prince's favor and during the Yongzhen era had greatly disrupted state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled how Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi—men of coarse character who had lingered at court awaiting summons—had won the crown prince's favor and, during the Yongzhen regency, had thrown government into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 是以訓導太子宮官，宜選正人。

translations.literal: Therefore those who instruct and guide the crown prince's household officials ought to be upright men.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he argued that those who instructed the crown prince's household should be men of upright character.

sentences.zh: 乃獻《教本書》曰：

translations.literal: He therefore presented a "Book on the Foundations of Instruction," which read:
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly submitted his "Book on the Foundations of Instruction," which began:

sentences.zh: 憲宗覽之甚悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong read it with great satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 又論西北邊事，皆朝政之大者。

translations.literal: He also discussed northwestern frontier matters—all major concerns of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed northwestern frontier affairs, each a matter of central importance to the court.

sentences.zh: 憲宗召對，問方略。

translations.literal: Xianzong summoned him for audience and asked his strategic views.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong summoned him for a private audience and questioned him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 為執政所忌，出為河南縣尉。

translations.literal: He was resented by those in power and was sent out as magistrate of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers took offense, and he was transferred out to serve as magistrate of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his mother and completing the requisite period, he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 四年，奉使東蜀，劾奏故劍南東川節度使嚴礪違制擅賦，又籍沒塗山甫等吏民八十八戶田宅一百一十一、奴婢二十七人、草千五百束、錢七千貫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was dispatched to eastern Shu and memorialized accusing the former military governor of Jiannan East, Yan Li, of violating regulations in levying unauthorized taxes, and of confiscating from officials and commoners including Tu Shanfu eighty-eight households' estates numbering one hundred and eleven, twenty-seven bondservants, fifteen hundred bundles of forage, and seven thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent on mission to eastern Shu and impeached the former military governor of eastern Sichuan, Yan Li, for unauthorized levies in violation of regulations. He further documented the confiscation of property from eighty-eight households of officials and commoners—including Tu Shanfu—totaling 111 parcels of land, 27 bondservants, 1,500 bundles of forage, and 7,000 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 時礪已死，七州刺史皆責罰。

translations.literal: Yan Li had already died; the prefects of seven prefectures were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li was already dead, but the governors of seven prefectures were all called to account and penalized.

sentences.zh: 稹雖舉職，而執政有與礪厚者惡之。

translations.literal: Though Zhen had performed his duties, someone among those in power who had been close to Yan Li bore him ill will.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhen had done his duty, certain powerful figures who had been on friendly terms with Yan Li turned against him.

sentences.zh: 使還，令分務東臺。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, he was ordered to divide duties at the eastern tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was assigned to share duties at the eastern office of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使韓臯封杖決湖州安吉令孫澥，四日內死。

translations.literal: Han Gao, surveillance commissioner of Zhexi, had Sun Xie, magistrate of Anji in Huzhou, beaten with the cudgel to death within four days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao, commissioner of Zhexi, had ordered Sun Xie, magistrate of Anji in Huzhou, beaten with the cudgel; Sun died within four days.

sentences.zh: 徐州監軍使孟升卒，節度使王紹傳送升喪柩還京，給券乘驛，仍於郵舍安喪柩。

translations.literal: When the army supervisor of Xuzhou, Meng Sheng, died, the military governor Wang Shao had Sheng's coffin escorted back to the capital, issued passes for relay transport, and even lodged the coffin at a postal station.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Sheng, the army supervisor at Xuzhou, died, the military governor Wang Shao had his coffin sent to the capital with relay passes and even housed the coffin overnight at a postal station—both grave breaches of protocol.

sentences.zh: 稹並劾奏以法。

translations.literal: Zhen impeached them both according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen impeached both men on legal grounds.

sentences.zh: 河南尹房式為不法事，稹欲追攝，擅令停務。

translations.literal: Fang Shi, intendant of Henan, had committed unlawful acts; Zhen wished to summon him for questioning, but Fang on his own authority ordered his office to cease operations.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shi, intendant of the Henan metropolitan district, had engaged in unlawful conduct; when Zhen sought to summon him, Fang unilaterally suspended his office's operations.

sentences.zh: 既飛表聞奏，罰式一月俸，仍召稹還京。

translations.literal: Fang hurried a memorial to the throne; Shi was fined one month's salary, and Zhen was nevertheless recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rushed a memorial to court; Shi was fined one month's salary, and Zhen was recalled to the capital nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 宿敷水驛，內官劉士元後至，爭廳。

translations.literal: He lodged at Fushui Post; the inner-court eunuch Liu Shiyuan arrived later and they disputed over the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: While staying at Fushui Post, he encountered the eunuch Liu Shiyuan, who had arrived later and contested possession of the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 士元怒，排其戶，稹襪而走廳後。

translations.literal: Shiyuan in anger burst through the door; Zhen fled in his stocking feet to the rear of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan flew into a rage, forced the door open, and Zhen fled barefoot to the rear of the hall.

sentences.zh: 士元追之，後以棰擊稹傷面。

translations.literal: Shiyuan pursued him and afterward struck Zhen in the face with a club.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan pursued him and struck him across the face with a club.

sentences.zh: 執政以稹少年後輩，務作威福，貶為江陵府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Those in power, regarding Zhen as a young junior who sought to wield authority for his own benefit, demoted him to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, deeming the young upstart bent on throwing his weight around, demoted him to staff officer in the Jiangling prefectural army.

sentences.zh: 稹聰警絕人，年少有才名，與太原白居易友善。

translations.literal: Zhen's intelligence surpassed others; in youth he had a reputation for talent and was on friendly terms with Bai Juyi of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was exceptionally quick-witted; even in youth he enjoyed a reputation for talent, and he formed a close friendship with Bai Juyi of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，善狀詠風態物色，當時言詩者，稱元、白焉。

translations.literal: He excelled at poetry and was skilled at depicting moods and scenes; those who spoke of poetry at the time paired Yuan and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at verse and had a gift for capturing mood and scenery; contemporaries who discussed poetry paired "Yuan and Bai."

sentences.zh: 自衣冠士子，至閭閻下俚，悉傳諷之，號為「元和體」。

translations.literal: From scholars in official dress down to commoners in the lanes, all recited and chanted his works, which were called the "Yuanhe style."
translations.idiomatic: From court gentlemen to common folk in the alleyways, everyone recited his poems; the style became known as the "Yuanhe manner."

sentences.zh: 既以俊爽不容於朝，流放荊蠻者僅十年。

translations.literal: Because his brilliance and candor were not tolerated at court, he was exiled to the southern barbarian lands for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His brilliance and outspokenness had made him unwelcome at court, and he spent nearly ten years in exile in the Jingnan region.

sentences.zh: 俄而白居易亦貶江州司馬，稹量移通州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long Bai Juyi was also demoted to marshal of Jiangzhou; Zhen was transferred in grade to marshal of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bai Juyi was demoted to marshal of Jiangzhou as well, while Zhen was transferred to the same post at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖通、江懸邈，而二人來往贈答。

translations.literal: Though Tong and Jiang were far apart, the two men exchanged visits and poetic gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tongzhou and Jiangzhou lay far apart, the two men exchanged visits and poems across the distance.

sentences.zh: 凡所為詩，有自三十、五十韻乃至百韻者。

translations.literal: Of the poems they composed, some ran from thirty or fifty rhymes to as many as a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Their poems ranged in length from thirty or fifty rhymes to as many as a hundred.

sentences.zh: 江南人士，傳道諷誦，流聞闕下，裏巷相傳，為之紙貴。

translations.literal: Gentlemen south of the Yangtze passed them along and chanted them; they flowed to the capital, were copied from lane to lane, and drove up the price of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in the south copied and recited them; the poems traveled to the capital, spread through every neighborhood, and drove up the price of paper.

sentences.zh: 觀其流離放逐之意，靡不淒惋。

translations.literal: Observing the sense of wandering banishment in them, none failed to find them poignant and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Readers found in them the ache of exile and displacement—every poem touched with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 十四年，自虢州長史征還，為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned back from his post as senior administrator of Guozhou and made vice director of the Catering Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recalled from senior administrator of Guozhou and appointed vice director in the Bureau of Foodstuffs.

sentences.zh: 宰相令狐楚一代文宗，雅知稹之辭學，謂稹曰：「嘗覽足下製作，所恨不多，遲之久矣。

translations.literal: The chief minister Linghu Chu, a literary authority of his generation, had long appreciated Zhen's literary learning and said to him: "I have read your compositions before; I regret there are not more of them, and I have waited too long.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu, the chief minister and a leading literary figure of the age, had long admired Zhen's literary gifts. He told him, "I have read your work before and regretted that there was not more of it; I have waited far too long.

sentences.zh: 請出其所有，以豁予情。」

translations.literal: Please bring out everything you have, so as to satisfy my feelings."
translations.idiomatic: Bring out everything you have written and satisfy my wish at last."

sentences.zh: 稹因獻其文，自敘曰：

translations.literal: Zhen thereupon presented his writings, with a preface that read:
translations.idiomatic: Zhen accordingly presented his collected writings, prefaced with an autobiographical note that read:

sentences.zh: 楚深稱賞，以為今代之鮑、謝也。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu praised them deeply, holding him the Bao and Xie of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu praised them extravagantly, declaring him the Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun of their generation.

sentences.zh: 穆宗皇帝在東宮，有妃嬪左右嘗誦稹歌詩以為樂曲者，知稹所為，嘗稱其善，宮中呼為元才子。

translations.literal: While Emperor Muzong was crown prince, concubines and attendants at his side had sometimes recited Zhen's songs as tunes; knowing Zhen's work, they had praised it, and within the palace he was called the Yuan talent.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Muzong was still crown prince, ladies of his household had sometimes sung Zhen's poems as songs; they knew his work and praised it, and within the palace he was called "the Yuan talent."

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍崔潭峻甚禮接稹，不以掾吏遇之，常征其詩什諷誦之。

translations.literal: The Jingnan army supervisor Cui Tanjun treated Zhen with great courtesy, not regarding him as a mere clerk, and often requested his poems to recite.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tanjun, army supervisor in Jingnan, treated Zhen with exceptional respect rather than as a lowly clerk, and often asked for his poems to recite.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，潭峻歸朝，出稹《連昌宮辭》等百餘篇奏御。

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era Tanjun returned to court and presented to the throne more than a hundred pieces including Zhen's "Ballad of the Lianchang Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing reign Tanjun returned to the capital and presented to the throne more than a hundred of Zhen's works, including "Ballad of the Lianchang Palace."

sentences.zh: 穆宗大悅，問稹安在。

translations.literal: Muzong was greatly pleased and asked where Zhen was.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was delighted and asked where Zhen was serving.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今為南宮散郎。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "He is now a junior gentleman of the Southern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "He is presently a junior gentleman of the Southern Palace."

sentences.zh: 即日轉祠部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: That same day he was transferred to director of the Sacrifices Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was transferred to director of the Sacrifices Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以書命不由相府，甚鄙之。

translations.literal: The court, because written commands had not come through the chancellery, regarded this with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The court looked down on the appointment because the edicts had not passed through the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 然辭誥所出，夐然與古為侔，遂盛傳於代，由是極承恩顧。

translations.literal: Yet the proclamations he drafted stood far apart from antiquity in their excellence and soon spread widely through the age; from this he received the utmost imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edicts he drafted matched the ancients in grandeur and spread swiftly through the realm, and from this he won extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《長慶宮辭》數十百篇，京師競相傳唱。

translations.literal: He once composed several dozen or hundred pieces of "Changqing Palace Lyrics," which the capital competed to sing.
translations.idiomatic: He composed dozens or hundreds of "Changqing Palace Lyrics," which the capital took up and sang in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 居無何，召入翰林，為中書舍人、承旨學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as drafting academician and chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as drafting academician and chief academician.

sentences.zh: 中人以潭峻之故，爭與稹交，而知樞密魏弘簡尤與稹相善，穆宗愈深知重。

translations.literal: Eunuchs, because of Tanjun, vied to befriend Zhen, and Wei Hongjian of the Bureau of Military Affairs was especially close to him; Muzong came to know and value him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Tanjun, eunuchs vied to befriend Zhen, and Wei Hongjian of the Bureau of Military Affairs was especially close to him; Muzong valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使裴度三上疏，言稹與弘簡為刎頸之交，謀亂朝政，言甚激訐。

translations.literal: The military governor of Hedong, Pei Du, submitted three memorials stating that Zhen and Hongjian were sworn friends plotting to disrupt court governance, with language fiercely accusatory.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, military governor of Hedong, submitted three memorials claiming that Zhen and Hongjian were sworn friends plotting to disrupt court governance, in fiercely accusatory language.

sentences.zh: 穆宗顧中外人情，乃罷稹內職，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Muzong, considering sentiment inside and outside the court, removed Zhen from his inner post and appointed him vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, weighing opinion within and outside the court, stripped Zhen of his inner-court post and made him vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 上恩顧未衰。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor for him had not yet waned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor had not yet waned.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，拜平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 詔下之日，朝野無不輕笑之。

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued, neither court nor populace could refrain from laughing lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, court and populace alike could scarcely suppress a smile.

sentences.zh: 時王廷湊、硃克融連兵圍牛元翼於深州，朝廷俱赦其罪，賜節鉞，令罷兵，俱不奉詔。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Tingcou and Zhu Keyi had joined forces to besiege Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; the court had pardoned their crimes and bestowed military commissions, ordering them to withdraw, but both refused the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Tingcou and Zhu Keyi had joined forces to besiege Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; the court had pardoned their crimes and granted them military commissions, ordering them to withdraw, but both refused the edicts.

sentences.zh: 稹以天子非次拔擢，欲有所立以報上。

translations.literal: Zhen, because the Son of Heaven had raised him out of turn, wished to accomplish something to repay his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, having been raised to office by an exceptional imperial favor, wished to accomplish something worthy in return.

sentences.zh: 有和王傅於方者，故司空頔之子，干進於稹。

translations.literal: There was a prince's tutor named Yu Fang, son of the former Minister of Works Yu Di, who pressed himself on Zhen for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's tutor named Yu Fang, son of the former Minister of Works Yu Di, pressed himself on Zhen seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 言有奇士王昭、王友明二人，嘗客於燕、趙間，頗與賊黨通熟，可以反間而出元翼。

translations.literal: He spoke of two extraordinary men, Wang Zhao and Wang Youming, who had lodged in Yan and Zhao and were well acquainted with the rebel bands, and who could be used in a stratagem to extricate Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of two men of unusual ability, Wang Zhao and Wang Youming, who had sojourned in the Yan and Zhao region and were well acquainted with the rebel factions, and who might be turned through counter-intelligence to rescue Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 仍自以家財資其行，仍賂兵吏部令史為出告身二十通，以便宜給賜，稹皆然之。

translations.literal: He offered his family wealth to fund their mission and bribed clerks in the Ministry of War to issue twenty blank commissions for discretionary reward; Zhen approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his family wealth to fund their mission and bribed clerks in the Ministry of War to issue twenty blank commissions for discretionary reward; Zhen approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 有李賞者，知於方之謀，以稹與裴度有隙，乃告度云：「於方為稹所使，欲結客王昭等刺度。」

translations.literal: One Li Shang, knowing of Fang's plot and aware of the rift between Zhen and Pei Du, reported to Du: "Yu Fang is acting at Zhen's behest, seeking to recruit Wang Zhao and others to assassinate Du."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Li Shang, who knew of Fang's scheme and aware of the rift between Zhen and Pei Du, reported to Du: "Yu Fang is acting at Zhen's orders, recruiting Wang Zhao and others to assassinate you."

sentences.zh: 度隱而不發。

translations.literal: Du kept silent and did not expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Du kept silent and did not act on the report.

sentences.zh: 及神策軍中尉奏於方之事，乃詔三司使韓臯等訊鞫，而害裴事無驗，而前事盡露。

translations.literal: When the director of the Divine Stratagem Army memorialized on Fang's affair, an edict ordered the three judicial offices under Han Gao and others to investigate; the charge against Pei was unverified, but the earlier matters came fully to light.
translations.idiomatic: When the director of the Divine Stratagem Army reported on Fang's affair, the three judicial offices under Han Gao and others were ordered to investigate; the plot against Pei could not be verified, but the earlier schemes were fully exposed.

sentences.zh: 遂俱罷稹、度平章事，乃出稹為同州刺史，度守僕射。

translations.literal: Zhen and Du were both removed as chief councilors; Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou and Du retained his post as vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhen and Du were removed as chief councilors; Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou while Du remained vice director.

sentences.zh: 諫官上疏，言責度太重，稹太輕。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials submitted memorials saying the punishment of Du was too heavy and that of Zhen too light.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials submitted memorials arguing that Du's punishment was too severe and Zhen's too lenient.

sentences.zh: 上心憐稹，止削長春宮使。

translations.literal: The emperor, pitying Zhen, only stripped him of his commission as commissioner of the Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taking pity on Zhen, only stripped him of his commission as commissioner of the Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 稹初罷相，三司獄未奏，京兆尹劉遵古遣坊所由潛邏稹居第，稹奏訴之。

translations.literal: When Zhen had first been removed as chief councilor, before the three offices had reported, the metropolitan intendant Liu Zungu sent ward officers to spy secretly on Zhen's residence; Zhen memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhen lost the chancellorship, before the three offices had concluded their report, the metropolitan intendant Liu Zungu sent ward officers to spy on Zhen's residence; Zhen memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 上怒，罰遵古，遣中人撫諭稹。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered, punished Zungu, and sent a eunuch to console Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered, punished Zungu, and dispatched a eunuch to console Zhen.

sentences.zh: 稹至同州，因表謝上，自敘曰：

translations.literal: When Zhen reached Tongzhou he submitted a memorial of thanks to the throne, with a self-account that read:
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Tongzhou he submitted a memorial of thanks to the throne, with a self-account that read:

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，改授越州刺史、兼御史大夫、漸東觀察使。

translations.literal: After two years in the prefecture he was reassigned as governor of Yuezhou with concurrent appointment as grand censor and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the prefecture he was reassigned as governor of Yuezhou with concurrent appointment as grand censor and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 會稽山水奇秀，稹所辟幕職，皆當時文士，而鏡湖、秦望之遊，月三四焉。

translations.literal: Kuaiji's mountains and waters were wondrously beautiful; the staff Zhen recruited were all literary men of the day, and excursions to Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang came three or four times a month.
translations.idiomatic: The landscape of Kuaiji was wondrously beautiful; the staff he recruited were all leading literary men of the day, and he toured Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang three or four times a month.

sentences.zh: 而諷詠詩什，動盈卷帙。

translations.literal: The poems he composed in response to occasions often filled whole scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The poems he composed on these outings often filled whole scrolls.

sentences.zh: 副使竇鞏，海內詩名，與稹酬唱最多，至今稱蘭亭絕唱。

translations.literal: His deputy Dou Gong, renowned throughout the realm for poetry, exchanged verses with Zhen more than any other; to this day their Lanting songs are called unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Dou Gong, renowned throughout the realm for poetry, exchanged verses with Zhen more than any other; to this day their Lanting songs are called unmatched.

sentences.zh: 稹既放意娛遊，稍不修邊幅，以瀆貨聞於時。

translations.literal: Zhen gave himself over to pleasure and travel and paid little heed to personal decorum, gaining a reputation for corrupt enrichment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen gave himself over to pleasure and travel and paid little heed to personal decorum, gaining a reputation for corrupt enrichment.

sentences.zh: 凡在越八年。

translations.literal: In all he spent eight years in Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Yue for eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 太和初，就加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe era he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year he entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 振舉紀綱，出郎官頗乖公議者七人。

translations.literal: He raised standards and regulations and removed seven bureau officials who had long fallen short of public consensus.
translations.idiomatic: He raised standards and regulations and removed seven bureau officials who had long fallen short of public consensus.

sentences.zh: 然以稹素無檢操，人情不厭服。

translations.literal: Yet because Zhen had never been restrained in conduct, popular sentiment did not willingly accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Zhen had never been restrained in conduct, popular sentiment did not willingly accept him.

sentences.zh: 會宰相王播倉卒而卒，稹大為路歧，經營相位。

translations.literal: When the chief minister Wang Bo died suddenly, Zhen went to great lengths along the road, maneuvering for the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister Wang Bo died suddenly, Zhen went to great lengths along the road, maneuvering for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，檢校戶部尚書，兼鄂州刺史、御史大夫、武昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Revenue with concurrent posts as governor of Ezhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Wuchang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Revenue with concurrent posts as governor of Ezhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Wuchang army.

sentences.zh: 五年七月二十二日暴疾，一日而卒於鎮，時年五十三，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the fifth year he was seized by sudden illness and died at his post within a day, at the age of fifty-three; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the fifth year he was seized by sudden illness and died at his post within a day, at the age of fifty-three; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有子曰道護，時年三歲。

translations.literal: He had a son named Daohu, then three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Daohu, then three years old.

sentences.zh: 稹仲兄司農少卿積，營護喪事。

translations.literal: Zhen's elder brother Ji, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, arranged the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's elder brother Ji, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦、詔冊、銘誄、論議等雜文一百卷，號曰《元氏長慶集》。

translations.literal: His collected poems, fu, edicts, inscriptions, eulogies, discourses, and miscellaneous prose fill one hundred scrolls, entitled Collected Writings of Master Yuan of the Changqing Era.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poems, fu, edicts, inscriptions, eulogies, discourses, and miscellaneous prose fill one hundred scrolls, entitled Collected Writings of Master Yuan of the Changqing Era.

sentences.zh: 又著古今刑政書三百卷，號《類集》，並行於代。

translations.literal: He also compiled three hundred scrolls on penal administration ancient and modern, entitled Classified Compilations, and both works circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled three hundred scrolls on penal administration ancient and modern, entitled Classified Compilations, and both works circulated widely in his age.

sentences.zh: 稹長慶末因編刪其文稿，《自敘》曰：

translations.literal: At the end of the Changqing era Zhen edited his manuscripts; his "Self-Account" reads:
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Changqing era Zhen edited his manuscripts; his "Self-Account" reads:

sentences.zh: 其自敘如此，欲知其作者之意，備於此篇。

translations.literal: His self-account is as above; those who wish to know the author's intent will find it fully set forth in that piece.
translations.idiomatic: His self-account is as above; those who wish to know the author's intent will find it fully set forth in that piece.

sentences.zh: 稹文友與白居易最善。

translations.literal: Among Zhen's literary friends, Bai Juyi was closest.
translations.idiomatic: Of Zhen's literary friends, none was closer than Bai Juyi.

sentences.zh: 後進之士，最重龐嚴，言其文體類己，保薦之。

translations.literal: Junior scholars held Pang Yan in highest regard, saying his literary style resembled Zhen's own, and Zhen recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger writers esteemed Pang Yan most highly, saying his style resembled Zhen's, and Zhen recommended him.

sentences.zh: 龐嚴龐嚴者，壽春人。

translations.literal: Pang Yan, Pang Yan, was a man of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Yan came from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 父景昭。

translations.literal: His father was Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 嚴元和中登進士第，長慶元年應制舉賢良方正、能直言極諫科，策入三等，冠制科之首。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi examination in the Yuanhe era; in the first year of Changqing he entered the special examination for worthy and upright men able to speak blunt remonstrance, his policy essay placing in the third grade and ranking first among those in the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yan passed the jinshi in the Yuanhe era; in the first year of Changqing he entered the special examination for worthy and upright men able to speak blunt remonstrance, placing third in grade and ranking first among the special-examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 是月，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: That month he was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 聰敏絕人，文章峭麗。

translations.literal: His intelligence surpassed others, and his writing was sharp and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally intelligent, and his prose was sharp and elegant.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士元稹、李紳頗知之。

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen knew him well.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen knew him well.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 轉左補闕，再遷駕部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer, then promoted again to director of the Carriages Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer, then promoted to director of the Carriages Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 嚴與右拾遺蔣防俱為稹、紳保薦，至諫官內職。

translations.literal: Yan and the Right Reminder Jiang Fang were both recommended by Zhen and Shen to remonstrance posts and inner-court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the Right Reminder Jiang Fang were both recommended by Zhen and Shen for remonstrance posts and inner-court offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，昭湣即位，李紳為宰相李逢吉所排，貶端州司馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Zhaomin ascended the throne; Li Shen was ousted by the chief minister Li Fengji and demoted to marshal of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Zhaomin ascended the throne, Li Shen was ousted by the chief minister Li Fengji and demoted to marshal of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴坐累，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan was implicated and sent out as governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was implicated by association and sent out as governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中於敖素與嚴善，制既下，敖封還，時人凜然相顧曰：「於給事犯宰相怒而為知己，不亦危乎！」

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Ao had long been friendly with Yan; once the appointment edict was issued, Ao sealed it and returned it, and people at court looked at one another in alarm and said: "Attendant Yu has offended the chief minister's wrath for the sake of a friend—is he not in peril?"
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Ao had long been friendly with Yan; when the appointment edict was issued, Ao sealed it and returned it, and people at court looked at one another in alarm and said, "Attendant Yu has offended the chief minister's wrath for a friend's sake—is he not in peril?"

sentences.zh: 及覆制出，乃知敖駁制書貶嚴太輕，中外無不嗤誚，以為口實。

translations.literal: When the revised edict was issued, it turned out Ao had rejected the draft as punishing Yan too lightly; inside and outside the court none failed to mock and cite it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: When the revised edict appeared, it turned out Ao had rejected the draft as punishing Yan too lightly; court and populace alike mocked the affair and made it a byword.

sentences.zh: 初李紳謫官，朝官皆賀逢吉，唯右拾遺吳思不賀。

translations.literal: When Li Shen was first demoted, court officials all congratulated Fengji; only the Right Reminder Wu Si did not congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shen was first demoted, court officials all congratulated Fengji; only the Right Reminder Wu Si refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 逢吉怒，改為殿中侍御史，充入蕃告哀使。

translations.literal: Fengji in anger transferred him to palace censor and appointed him envoy to announce mourning in a foreign land.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji in anger transferred him to palace censor and appointed him envoy to announce mourning in a foreign land.

sentences.zh: 嚴復入為庫部郎中。

translations.literal: Yan was recalled and made director of the Storehouses Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was recalled and made director of the Storehouses Bureau.

sentences.zh: 太和二年二月，上試制舉人，命嚴與左散騎常侍馮宿、太常少卿賈餗為試官，以裴休為甲等制科之首。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Taihe the emperor tested special-examination candidates and appointed Yan, together with the Left Regular Attendant Feng Su and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jia Su, as examiners, with Pei Xiu ranking first in the top grade of the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Taihe the emperor tested special-examination candidates and appointed Yan, together with the Left Regular Attendant Feng Su and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jia Su, as examiners, with Pei Xiu ranking first in the top grade of the special examination.

sentences.zh: 有應直言極諫舉人劉蕡，條對激切，凡數千言。

translations.literal: There was a candidate in the blunt remonstrance examination, Liu Fen, whose itemized responses were fiercely incisive, running to several thousand words in all.
translations.idiomatic: Among the candidates for blunt remonstrance was Liu Fen, whose itemized responses were fiercely incisive, running to several thousand words in all.

sentences.zh: 不中選，人鹹以為屈。

translations.literal: He was not selected, and people all regarded it as unjust.
translations.idiomatic: He was not selected, and people widely regarded it as unjust.

sentences.zh: 其所對策，大行於時，登科者有請以身名授蕡者。

translations.literal: His policy essay circulated greatly at the time, and among those who had passed the examination some asked to yield their fame to Fen.
translations.idiomatic: His policy essay circulated widely at the time, and some who had passed the examination offered to yield their fame to Fen.

sentences.zh: 嚴再遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Yan was promoted again to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was promoted again to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，權知京兆尹，以強幹不避權豪稱，然無士君子之檢操，貪勢嗜利。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as acting metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, praised for being forceful and unafraid of powerful families, yet he lacked the restraint of a gentleman-scholar and was greedy for power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as acting metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, praised for being forceful and unafraid of powerful families, yet he lacked a gentleman-scholar's restraint and was greedy for power and profit.

sentences.zh: 因醉而卒。

translations.literal: He died of drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in a drunken stupor.

sentences.zh: 白居易白居易，字樂天，太原人。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi, Bai Juyi, style name Letian, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi, whose courtesy name was Letian, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 北齊五兵尚書建之仍孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Jian of the Northern Qi, who had been Minister of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Jian, Minister of the Five Armies under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 建生士通，皇朝利州都督。

translations.literal: Jian begot Shitong, military governor of Lizhou in the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian begot Shitong, who served as military governor of Lizhou in the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 士通生志善，尚衣奉御。

translations.literal: Shitong begot Zhishan, Attendant for Imperial Vestments.
translations.idiomatic: Shitong begot Zhishan, Attendant for Imperial Vestments.

sentences.zh: 志善生溫，檢校都官郎中。

translations.literal: Zhishan begot Wen, acting director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan begot Wen, acting director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 溫生锽，歷酸棗、鞏二縣令。

translations.literal: Wen begot Huang, who served in turn as magistrate of Suozao and Gong counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wen begot Huang, who served in turn as magistrate of Suozao and Gong counties.

sentences.zh: 锽生季庚，建中初為彭城令。

translations.literal: Huang begot Jigeng, who in the early Jianzhong era was magistrate of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang begot Jigeng, who in the early Jianzhong era was magistrate of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時李正己據河南十餘州叛。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhengji held more than ten prefectures south of the Yellow River in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zhengji held more than ten prefectures south of the Yellow River in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 正己宗人洧為徐州刺史，季庚說洧以彭門歸國，因授朝散大夫、大理少卿、徐州別駕，賜緋魚袋，兼徐泗觀察判官。

translations.literal: Zhengji's clansman Wei was military governor of Xuzhou; Jigeng persuaded Wei to return Pengmen to the state, and for this he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Xuzhou vice governor, a crimson fish bag, and concurrent appointment as administrative aide to the Xuzhou-Si surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji's clansman Wei was military governor of Xuzhou; Jigeng persuaded Wei to return Pengmen to the state, and for this he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Xuzhou vice governor, a crimson fish bag, and concurrent appointment as administrative aide to the Xuzhou-Si surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷衢州、襄州別駕。

translations.literal: He served in turn as vice governor of Quzhou and Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice governor of Quzhou and Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自锽至季庚，世敦儒業，皆以明經出身。

translations.literal: From Huang down to Jigeng, the family cultivated Confucian learning for generations, all entering office through the Classics examinations.
translations.idiomatic: From Huang down to Jigeng, the family cultivated Confucian learning for generations, all entering office through the Classics examinations.

sentences.zh: 季庚生居易。

translations.literal: Jigeng begot Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng begot Juyi.

sentences.zh: 初，建立功於高齊，賜田於韓城，子孫家焉，遂移籍同州。

translations.literal: At first Jian had rendered meritorious service to the Northern Qi and was granted fields in Hancheng; the family settled there and later transferred their registry to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jian had rendered meritorious service to the Northern Qi and was granted fields in Hancheng; the family settled there and later transferred their registry to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 至溫徙於下邽，今為下邽人焉。

translations.literal: When Wen moved to Xiaji, they became men of Xiaji; today they are registered as men of Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen moved to Xiaji, the family settled there; today they are registered as men of Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 居易幼聰慧絕人，襟懷宏放。

translations.literal: Juyi in youth was exceptionally intelligent, with a broad and expansive spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi in youth was exceptionally intelligent, with a broad and expansive spirit.

sentences.zh: 年十五六時，袖文一編，投著作郎吳人顧況。

translations.literal: When he was fifteen or sixteen he tucked a literary manuscript under his sleeve and presented it to Gu Kuang, a native of Wu who was an editorial director.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fifteen or sixteen he tucked a literary manuscript under his sleeve and presented it to Gu Kuang, a native of Wu who was an editorial director.

sentences.zh: 況能文，而性浮薄，後進文章無可意者。

translations.literal: Kuang could write but was by nature frivolous; he found nothing satisfactory in the writings of junior scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang could write but was by nature frivolous; he found nothing satisfactory in the writings of junior scholars.

sentences.zh: 覽居易文，不覺迎門禮遇，曰：「吾謂斯文遂絕，復得吾子矣。」

translations.literal: Reading Juyi's essay, he could not help but go out to the gate to receive him with courtesy and said: "I thought this literary tradition had perished; I have found you again."
translations.idiomatic: Reading Juyi's essay, he could not help but go out to the gate to receive him with courtesy and said, "I thought this literary tradition had perished; I have found you again."

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，始以進士就試，禮部侍郎高郢擢升甲科，吏部判入等，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he first took the jinshi examination; Vice Director of Rites Gao Ying elevated him to the top grade, the Ministry of Personnel assessment placed him in grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he first took the jinshi examination; Vice Director of Rites Gao Ying elevated him to the top grade, the Ministry of Personnel assessment placed him in grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 元和元年四月，憲宗策試制舉人，應才識兼茂、明於體用科，策入第四等，授盩厔縣慰、集賢校理。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe Emperor Xianzong tested special-examination candidates; Juyi entered the examination for outstanding talent and practical understanding, his policy placing in the fourth grade, and he was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe Emperor Xianzong tested special-examination candidates; Juyi entered the examination for outstanding talent and practical understanding, his policy placing in the fourth grade, and he was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 居易文辭富艷，尤精於詩筆。

translations.literal: Juyi's literary compositions were rich and gorgeous, and he was especially skilled in poetic writing.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's literary compositions were rich and gorgeous, and he was especially skilled in poetic writing.

sentences.zh: 自讎校至結綬畿甸，所著歌詩數十百篇，皆意存諷賦，箴時之病，補政之缺。

translations.literal: From proofreading through receiving his sash in the capital region, the songs and poems he composed numbered dozens or hundreds, all intending satirical expression, admonishing the ills of the age and repairing the gaps in governance.
translations.idiomatic: From proofreading through receiving his sash in the capital region, the songs and poems he composed numbered dozens or hundreds, all intending satirical expression, admonishing the ills of the age and repairing the gaps in governance.

sentences.zh: 而士君子多之，而往往流聞禁中。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and scholars mostly approved of them, and they often flowed into hearsay within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and scholars mostly approved of them, and they often reached the ears of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 章武皇帝納諫思理，渴聞讜言，二年十一月，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangwu, wishing to receive remonstrance and ponder governance, was eager to hear blunt counsel; in the eleventh month of the second year he summoned Juyi into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangwu, wishing to receive remonstrance and ponder governance, was eager to hear blunt counsel; in the eleventh month of the second year he summoned Juyi into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year he was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 居易自以逢好文之主，非次拔擢，欲以生平所貯，仰酬恩造。

translations.literal: Juyi considered that he had encountered a sovereign who loved literature and had been raised out of turn; he wished to offer up what he had stored through his life to repay the grace of his elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi considered that he had encountered a sovereign who loved literature and had been raised out of turn; he wished to offer up what he had stored through his life to repay the grace of his elevation.

sentences.zh: 拜命之日，獻疏言事曰：

translations.literal: On the day he received his appointment he submitted a memorial setting forth his views, which read:
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received his appointment he submitted a memorial setting forth his views, which read:

sentences.zh: 居易與河南元稹相善，同年登制舉，交情隆厚。

translations.literal: Juyi was on friendly terms with Yuan Zhen of Henan; they had passed the special examination in the same year and their friendship was deep and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi was on friendly terms with Yuan Zhen of Henan; they had passed the special examination in the same year and their friendship was deep and thick.

sentences.zh: 稹自監察御史謫為江陵府士曹掾，翰林學士李絳、崔群上前面論稹無罪，居易累疏切諫曰：

translations.literal: When Zhen was demoted from investigating censor to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture, Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun spoke to the emperor's face arguing that Zhen was guiltless; Juyi submitted memorial after memorial in blunt remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was demoted from investigating censor to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture, Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun spoke to the emperor's face arguing that Zhen was guiltless; Juyi submitted memorial after memorial in blunt remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 疏入不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial entered and received no response.

sentences.zh: 又淄青節度使李師道進絹，為魏徵子孫贖宅。

translations.literal: Also the military governor of Ziqing, Li Shidao, presented silk to ransom the residence of Wei Zheng's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Also the military governor of Ziqing, Li Shidao, presented silk to ransom the residence of Wei Zheng's descendants.

sentences.zh: 居易諫曰：「徵是陛下先朝宰相，太宗嘗賜殿材成其正室，尤與諸家第宅不同。

translations.literal: Juyi remonstrated, saying: "Wei was a chief minister of Your Majesty's former reign; Taizong once bestowed hall timber to complete his main hall, and it was especially unlike the mansions of other families.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi remonstrated, saying, "Wei was a chief minister of Your Majesty's former reign; Taizong once bestowed hall timber to complete his main hall, and it was especially unlike the mansions of other families.

sentences.zh: 子孫典貼，其錢不多，自可官中為之收贖，而令師道掠美，事實非宜。」

translations.literal: The descendants pawned it; the sum was not large and the court itself could redeem it, yet to let Shidao seize the credit is in truth not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The descendants pawned it; the sum was not large and the court itself could redeem it, yet to let Shidao seize the credit is in truth not fitting."

sentences.zh: 憲宗深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 上又欲加河東王鍔平章事，居易諫曰：「宰相是陛下輔臣，非賢良不可當此位。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to add Wang E of Hedong as chief councilor; Juyi remonstrated, saying: "The chief councilor is Your Majesty's assisting minister; only the worthy and good should hold this post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to add Wang E of Hedong as chief councilor; Juyi remonstrated, saying, "The chief councilor is Your Majesty's assisting minister; only the worthy and good should hold this post.

sentences.zh: 鍔誅剝民財，以市恩澤，不可使四方之人謂陛下得王鍔進奉，而與之宰相，深無益於聖朝。」

translations.literal: E strips the people's wealth to purchase favor; it must not be allowed that people in the four directions say Your Majesty received Wang E's tribute offerings and gave him the chancellorship—this is deeply without benefit to the holy court."
translations.idiomatic: E strips the people's wealth to purchase favor; it must not be allowed that people in the four directions say Your Majesty received Wang E's tribute offerings and gave him the chancellorship—this is deeply without benefit to the holy court."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And so it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 王承宗拒命，上令神策中尉吐突承璀為招討使，諫官上章者十七八。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong defied orders; the emperor appointed the director of the Divine Stratagem Army, Tuoba Chenghuan, as campaign commissioner, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials numbering seventeen or eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong defied orders; the emperor appointed the director of the Divine Stratagem Army, Tuoba Chenghuan, as campaign commissioner, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials numbering seventeen or eighteen.

sentences.zh: 居易面論，辭情切至。

translations.literal: Juyi argued face to face, his words urgent and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi argued face to face, his words urgent and sincere.

sentences.zh: 既而又請罷河北用兵，凡數千百言，皆人之難言者，上多聽納。

translations.literal: Afterward he again requested withdrawal of troops in Hebei; in all several thousand words, all things difficult for others to speak, and the emperor mostly listened and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he again requested withdrawal of troops in Hebei; in all several thousand words, all things difficult for others to speak, and the emperor mostly listened and accepted.

sentences.zh: 唯諫承璀事切，上頗不悅，謂李絳曰：「白居易小子，是朕拔擢致名位，而無禮於朕，朕實難奈。」

translations.literal: Only on the matter of remonstrating against Chenghuan was the emperor somewhat displeased, and he said to Li Jiang: "Bai Juyi the youngster is one I raised and elevated to fame and position, yet he is without propriety toward me—I truly find it hard to bear."
translations.idiomatic: Only on the matter of remonstrating against Chenghuan was the emperor somewhat displeased, and he said to Li Jiang, "Bai Juyi the youngster is one I raised and elevated to fame and position, yet he is without propriety toward me—I truly find it hard to bear."

sentences.zh: 絳對曰：「居易所以不避死亡之誅，事無巨細必言者，蓋酬陛下特力拔擢耳，非輕言也。

translations.literal: Jiang replied: "The reason Juyi does not avoid the punishment of death and speaks on matters great and small is that he is repaying Your Majesty's special elevation of him by force—it is not light speech.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied, "The reason Juyi does not avoid the punishment of death and speaks on matters great and small is that he is repaying Your Majesty's special elevation of him by force—it is not light speech.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲開諫諍之路，不宜阻居易言。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to open the path of blunt remonstrance; you should not obstruct Juyi's words."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to open the path of blunt remonstrance; you should not obstruct Juyi's words."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words are correct."

sentences.zh: 由是多見聽納。

translations.literal: From this Juyi was often heard and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: From this Juyi was often heard and accepted.

sentences.zh: 五年，當改官，上謂崔群曰：「居易官卑俸薄，拘於資地，不能超等，其官可聽自便奏來。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his term for office change came due, the emperor said to Cui Qun: "Juyi's office is low and his salary thin; constrained by seniority he cannot be promoted beyond grade—his office may be reported as he himself wishes."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when his term for office change came due, the emperor said to Cui Qun, "Juyi's office is low and his salary thin; constrained by seniority he cannot be promoted beyond grade—his office may be reported as he himself wishes."

sentences.zh: 居易奏曰：「臣聞姜公輔為內職，求為京府判司，為奉親也。

translations.literal: Juyi memorialized, saying: "I have heard that Jiang Gongfu, holding an inner post, requested appointment as administrative aide in the capital prefecture for the sake of supporting his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi memorialized, saying, "I have heard that Jiang Gongfu, holding an inner post, requested appointment as administrative aide in the capital prefecture for the sake of supporting his parents.

sentences.zh: 臣有老母，家貧養薄，乞如公輔例。」

translations.literal: I have an aged mother; our household is poor and support is thin—I beg to follow Gongfu's example."
translations.idiomatic: I have an aged mother; our household is poor and support is thin—I beg to follow Gongfu's example."

sentences.zh: 於是，除京兆府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed army staff officer in the metropolitan prefecture's revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed army staff officer in the metropolitan prefecture's revenue section.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，丁母陳夫人之喪，退居下邽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother Lady Chen and retired to Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother Lady Chen and retired to Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，入朝，授太子左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he entered court and was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year he entered court and was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，盜殺宰相武元衡，居易首上疏論其冤，急請捕賊以雪國恥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year bandits killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng; Juyi was first to submit a memorial on his injustice and urgently requested capture of the assassins to wash away the national shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year bandits killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng; Juyi was first to submit a memorial on his injustice and urgently requested capture of the assassins to wash away the national shame.

sentences.zh: 宰相以宮官非諫職，不當先諫官言事。

translations.literal: The chief ministers held that a palace official was not a remonstrance post and ought not speak before remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers held that a palace official was not a remonstrance post and ought not speak before remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 會有素惡居易者，掎摭居易，言浮華無行，其母因看花墮井而死，而居易作《賞花》及《新井》詩，甚傷名教，不宜置彼周行。

translations.literal: There happened to be one who had long disliked Juyi; he seized on Juyi and said he was frivolous and without conduct—that his mother had died from falling into a well while viewing flowers, yet Juyi composed "Viewing Flowers" and "The New Well," gravely injuring moral teaching, and was unfit to stand among the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be one who had long disliked Juyi; he seized on Juyi and said he was frivolous and without conduct—that his mother had died from falling into a well while viewing flowers, yet Juyi composed "Viewing Flowers" and "The New Well," gravely injuring moral teaching, and was unfit to stand among the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 執政方惡其言事，奏貶為江表刺史。

translations.literal: Those in power at the time detested his remonstrances and memorialized that he be demoted to prefect south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power at the time detested his remonstrances and memorialized that he be demoted to prefect south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 詔出，中書舍人王涯上疏論之，言居易所犯狀跡，不宜治郡，追詔授江州司馬。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Drafting Academician Wang Ya submitted a memorial on the matter, saying that given the nature of Juyi's offenses he was unfit to govern a prefecture; the edict was recalled and he was appointed marshal of Jiangzhou instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Drafting Academician Wang Ya submitted a memorial on the matter, saying that given the nature of Juyi's offenses he was unfit to govern a prefecture; the edict was recalled and he was appointed marshal of Jiangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 居易儒學之外，尤通釋典，常以忘懷處順為事，都不以遷謫介意。

translations.literal: Beyond Confucian learning Juyi was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures and often took forgetting cares and accepting circumstances as his practice, not minding exile and demotion at all.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Confucian learning Juyi was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures and often took forgetting cares and accepting circumstances as his practice, not minding exile and demotion at all.

sentences.zh: 在湓城，立隱舍於廬山遺愛寺，嘗與人書言之曰：「予去年秋始遊廬山，到東西二林間香爐峰下，見雲木泉石，勝絕第一。

translations.literal: At Xuncheng he established a hermitage at the Jian'ai Temple on Mount Lu and once wrote to someone, saying: "Last autumn I first traveled Mount Lu; between the eastern and western forests at the foot of Incense Burner Peak I saw clouds, trees, springs, and rocks surpassing all else in excellence.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuncheng he established a hermitage at the Jian'ai Temple on Mount Lu and once wrote to someone, saying, "Last autumn I first traveled Mount Lu; between the eastern and western forests at the foot of Incense Burner Peak I saw clouds, trees, springs, and rocks surpassing all else in excellence.

sentences.zh: 愛不能舍，因立草堂。

translations.literal: I loved it and could not leave; therefore I built a thatched hall.
translations.idiomatic: I loved it and could not leave; therefore I built a thatched hall.

sentences.zh: 前有喬松十數株，修竹千餘竿，青羅為墻援，白石為橋道，流水周於舍下，飛泉落於檐間，紅榴白蓮，羅生池砌。」

translations.literal: Before it were more than ten tall pines, more than a thousand bamboo poles, green silk for a wall enclosure, white stone for a bridge path, flowing water circling below the lodge, flying springs falling between the eaves, red pomegranate and white lotus growing thick around the pool ledge."
translations.idiomatic: Before it were more than ten tall pines, more than a thousand bamboo poles, green silk for a wall enclosure, white stone for a bridge path, flowing water circling below the lodge, flying springs falling between the eaves, red pomegranate and white lotus growing thick around the pool ledge."

sentences.zh: 居易與湊、滿、朗、晦四禪師，追永、遠、宗、雷之跡，為人外之交。

translations.literal: Juyi with the four Chan masters Cou, Man, Lang, and Hui pursued the traces of Yong, Yuan, Zong, and Lei and formed friendships outside the world of men.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi with the four Chan masters Cou, Man, Lang, and Hui pursued the traces of Yong, Yuan, Zong, and Lei and formed friendships outside the world of men.

sentences.zh: 每相摧遊詠，躋危登險，極林泉之幽邃。

translations.literal: They often urged one another to travel and chant, climbing peril and ascending heights, reaching the utmost seclusion of forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: They often urged one another to travel and chant, climbing peril and ascending heights, reaching the utmost seclusion of forests and springs.

sentences.zh: 至於翛然順適之際，幾欲忘其形骸。

translations.literal: When they arrived at a state of free and easy accord, they nearly forgot their own bodies.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived at a state of free and easy accord, they nearly forgot their own bodies.

sentences.zh: 或經時不歸，或逾月而返，郡守以朝貴遇之，不之責。

translations.literal: Sometimes they did not return for a whole season, or returned only after more than a month; the prefect treated them as court nobility and did not hold them accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they did not return for a whole season, or returned only after more than a month; the prefect treated them as court nobility and did not hold them accountable.

sentences.zh: 時元稹在通州，篇詠贈答往來，不以數千里為遠。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen was in Tongzhou; poems exchanged in gift and response traveled back and forth, not considering several thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen was in Tongzhou; poems exchanged in gift and response traveled back and forth, not considering several thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 嘗與稹書，因論作文之大旨曰：

translations.literal: He once wrote to Zhen, and in discussing the great principles of writing said:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Zhen, and in discussing the great principles of writing said:

sentences.zh: 居易自敘如此，文士以為信然。

translations.literal: Juyi's self-account is as above; literary men regarded it as trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's self-account is as above; literary men regarded it as trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，量移忠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was transferred in grade to governor of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was transferred in grade to governor of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 自潯陽浮江上峽。

translations.literal: From Xunyang he floated upriver on the Yangtze into the gorges.
translations.idiomatic: From Xunyang he floated upriver on the Yangtze into the gorges.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，元稹會居易於峽口，停舟夷陵三日。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year Yuan Zhen met Juyi at the gorge mouth and moored their boats at Yiling for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year Yuan Zhen met Juyi at the gorge mouth and moored their boats at Yiling for three days.

sentences.zh: 時季弟行簡從行，三人於峽州西二十里黃牛峽口石洞中，置酒賦詩，戀戀不能訣。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brother Xingjian was traveling with him; the three men at a stone cave twenty li west of Yiling at the mouth of Yellow Ox Gorge set out wine and composed poems, reluctant to part and unable to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger brother Xingjian was traveling with him; the three men at a stone cave twenty li west of Yiling at the mouth of Yellow Ox Gorge set out wine and composed poems, reluctant to part and unable to take leave.

sentences.zh: 南賓郡當峽路之深險處也，花木多奇。

translations.literal: Nanbin prefecture lies at the deepest peril of the gorge route, and its flowers and trees are mostly extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Nanbin prefecture lies at the deepest peril of the gorge route, and its flowers and trees are mostly extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 居易在郡，為《木蓮荔枝圖》，寄朝中親友，各記其狀曰：「荔枝生巴、峽間，形圓如帷蓋。

translations.literal: While in the prefecture Juyi composed "Illustrations of Magnolia and Lychee" and sent them to kin and friends at court, each recording their forms, which read: "The lychee grows between Ba and the gorges; its form is round like a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: While in the prefecture Juyi composed "Illustrations of Magnolia and Lychee" and sent them to kin and friends at court, each recording their forms, which read, "The lychee grows between Ba and the gorges; its form is round like a canopy.

sentences.zh: 葉如桂，冬青；

translations.literal: Its leaves are like cassia, evergreen in winter;
translations.idiomatic: Its leaves are like cassia, evergreen in winter;

sentences.zh: 華如橘，春榮；

translations.literal: Its flowers are like the orange, blooming in spring;
translations.idiomatic: Its blossoms resemble the orange, opening in spring;

sentences.zh: 實如丹，夏熟。

translations.literal: Its fruit is like cinnabar, ripening in summer.
translations.idiomatic: Its fruit is like cinnabar, ripening in summer.

sentences.zh: 朵如蒲萄，核如枇杷，殼如紅繒，膜如紫綃，瓤肉瑩白如雪，漿液甘酸如醴酪。

translations.literal: Its clusters are like grapes, its pit like loquat, its shell like red silk gauze, its membrane like purple gauze, its flesh lustrous white as snow, its juice sweet and sour like fermented milk.
translations.idiomatic: Clusters hang like grapes; the pit resembles a loquat; the shell is red silk gauze, the membrane purple gauze; the flesh gleams white as snow; the juice is sweet-sour as cultured curds.

sentences.zh: 大略如此，其實過之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking it is thus, and in reality it surpasses this description.
translations.idiomatic: That is the general picture—and the fruit itself surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 若離本枝，一日而色變，二日而香變，三日而味變，四五日外，色香味盡去矣。」

translations.literal: If separated from its branch, in one day its color changes, in two days its fragrance changes, in three days its flavor changes, and beyond four or five days its color, fragrance, and flavor are all gone."
translations.idiomatic: If separated from its branch, in one day its color changes, in two days its fragrance changes, in three days its flavor changes, and beyond four or five days its color, fragrance, and flavor are all gone."

sentences.zh: 「木蓮大者高四五丈，巴民呼為黃心樹，經冬不雕。

translations.literal: "The magnolia large ones reach four or five zhang in height; the people of Ba call it the yellow-heart tree, and it does not wither through winter.
translations.idiomatic: The magnolia grows as tall as four or five zhang; Ba people call it the yellow-heart tree and it never sheds in winter.

sentences.zh: 身如青楊，有白文。

translations.literal: Its trunk is like green poplar, with white markings.
translations.idiomatic: Its trunk is like green poplar, with white markings.

sentences.zh: 葉如桂，厚大無脊。

translations.literal: Its leaves are like cassia, thick and large without a midrib.
translations.idiomatic: Its leaves are like cassia, thick and large without a midrib.

sentences.zh: 花如蓮，香色艷膩皆同，房獨蕊有異。

translations.literal: Its flowers are like the lotus; fragrance, color, and lush beauty are all the same, only the calyx and solitary pistil differ.
translations.idiomatic: Its flowers are like the lotus; fragrance, color, and lush beauty are all the same, only the calyx and solitary pistil differ.

sentences.zh: 四月初始開，自開迨謝，僅二十日。

translations.literal: It first opens in the fourth month; from opening until fading is only twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: It first opens in the fourth month; from opening until fading is only twenty days.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年夏，命道士毋丘元志寫之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he ordered the Daoist priest Wuqiu Yuanzhi to paint them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he ordered the Daoist priest Wuqiu Yuanzhi to paint them.

sentences.zh: 惜其遐僻，因以三絕賦之。」

translations.literal: Pitying their remote seclusion, he therefore composed a fu in three parts on them."
translations.idiomatic: Pitying their remote seclusion, he therefore composed a fu in three parts on them."

sentences.zh: 有「天教拋擲在深山」之句，鹹傳於都下，好事者喧然模寫。

translations.literal: There was the line "Heaven decreed them cast away deep in the mountains," which all transmitted in the capital, and enthusiasts clamored to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: Among its lines was "Heaven cast them off deep in the mountains," which swept through the capital until enthusiasts clamored to copy it.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，召還京師，拜司門員外郎。

translations.literal: That winter he was summoned back to the capital and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was summoned back to the capital and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉主客郎中、知制誥，加朝散大夫，始著緋。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to director of the Guests Bureau with charge of drafting edicts, granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and for the first time wore crimson.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to director of the Guests Bureau with charge of drafting edicts, granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and for the first time wore crimson.

sentences.zh: 時元稹亦征還為尚書郎、知制誥，同在綸閣。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen was also summoned back as director in a ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and both were together in the drafting pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen was also summoned back as director in a ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and both were together in the drafting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年三月，受詔與中書舍人王起覆，試禮部侍郎錢徽下及第人鄭朗等一十四人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Changqing he received an edict together with Drafting Academician Wang Qi to review the fourteen men including Zheng Lang whom Vice Director of Rites Qian Hui had passed in the lower examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Changqing he received an edict together with Drafting Academician Wang Qi to review the fourteen men including Zheng Lang whom Vice Director of Rites Qian Hui had passed in the lower examination.

sentences.zh: 十月，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to drafting academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was transferred to drafting academician.

sentences.zh: 十一月，穆宗親試制舉人，又與賈餗、陳岵為考策官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Emperor Muzong personally tested special-examination candidates, and Juyi again served with Jia Su and Chen Hu as policy examiners.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Emperor Muzong personally tested special-examination candidates, and Juyi again served with Jia Su and Chen Hu as policy examiners.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷文字之職，無不首居其選，然多為排擯，不得用其才。

translations.literal: Of all court posts for written composition, none failed to place him first in selection, yet he was often ostracized and could not employ his talents.
translations.idiomatic: Of all court posts for written composition, none failed to place him first in selection, yet he was often ostracized and could not employ his talents.

sentences.zh: 時天子荒縱不法，執政非其人，制御乖方，河朔復亂。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was dissolute and lawless, those in power were not the right men, regulation and control were misaligned, and Hebei again fell into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Son of Heaven was dissolute and lawless, those in power were not the right men, regulation and control were misaligned, and Hebei again fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 居易累上疏論其事，天子不能用，乃求外任。

translations.literal: Juyi submitted memorial after memorial discussing these matters; the Son of Heaven could not employ them, and Juyi then sought an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi submitted memorial after memorial discussing these matters; the Son of Heaven could not employ them, and Juyi then sought an outer appointment.

sentences.zh: 七月，除杭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed governor of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed governor of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而元稹罷相，自馮翊轉浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Zhen was removed as chief councilor and transferred from Fengyi to surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Zhen was removed as chief councilor and transferred from Fengyi to surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 交契素深，杭、越鄰境，篇詠往來，不間旬浹。

translations.literal: Their bond of friendship had always been deep; Hang and Yue were neighboring jurisdictions, and poems exchanged in gift and response came without a break of ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Their bond of friendship had always been deep; Hang and Yue were neighboring jurisdictions, and poems exchanged in gift and response came without a break of ten days.

sentences.zh: 嘗會於境上，數日而別。

translations.literal: They once met on the border and parted after several days.
translations.idiomatic: They once met on the border and parted after several days.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除太子左庶子，分司東都。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，復出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Baoli era he was again sent out as governor of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoli era he was again sent out as governor of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，征拜秘書監，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Juyi was summoned as Director of the Palace Library and granted the gold-purple seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Juyi was summoned as Director of the Palace Library and granted the gold-purple seal.

sentences.zh: 九月上誕節，召居易與僧惟澄、道土趙常盈對御講論於麟德殿。

translations.literal: On the imperial birthday in the ninth month he summoned Juyi together with the monk Weicheng and the Daoist Zhao Changying to lecture before the throne in the Qinde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial birthday in the ninth month he summoned Juyi together with the monk Weicheng and the Daoist Zhao Changying to lecture before the throne in the Qinde Hall.

sentences.zh: 居易論難鋒起，辭辨泉註，上疑宿構，深嗟挹之。

translations.literal: Juyi's disputations rose like spears and his eloquence poured like a spring; the emperor suspected he had prepared them beforehand and deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's rebuttals flashed like spears and his eloquence poured forth; the emperor suspected prepared answers and marveled at his mastery.

sentences.zh: 太和二年正月，轉刑部侍郎，封晉陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taihe he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments, enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taihe he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments, enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三年，稱病東歸，求為分司官，尋除太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year he claimed illness and returned east, requesting a duty-at-large post, and soon was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he claimed illness and returned east, requesting a duty-at-large post, and soon was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 居易初對策高第，擢入翰林，蒙英主特達顧遇，頗欲奮厲效報，茍致身於訏謨之地，則兼濟生靈，蓄意未果，望風為當路者所擠，流徙江湖。

translations.literal: When Juyi first answered policy at the top grade and was elevated into the Hanlin Academy, he received the special favor of an enlightened sovereign and wished earnestly to repay it; if he could reach a place of state counsel, he would benefit the people as well—but his intent was not realized; seeing the wind, those in power ostracized him and he was cast to the rivers and lakes.
